The problem: when redirect_stdout=True, sys.stdout is replaced with FileProxy, which lacks fileno attribute, so subprocess.Popen expects stdout to have fileno; FileProxy inherits from io.TextIOBase which by default doesn't implement fileno, so calling fileno raises UnsupportedOperation. The issue suggests adding fileno method to FileProxy that proxies to original file, or maybe implement fileno property via get_fileno in console? In Console _stdout handling they have get_fileno use. But FileProxy should expose fileno if underlying file has it. So modify rich/file_proxy.py to implement fileno method delegating to self.__file.fileno() if exists, also maybe isatty, readable etc. Already __getattr__ delegates unknown attributes, but fileno is a method defined on the underlying file but hidden because __getattr__ handles attribute lookups only for missing attributes, not for methods defined on the class. Since FileProxy does not define fileno, __getattr__ should return getattr(self.__file, 'fileno'), so calling sys.stdout.fileno() should work? Wait, __getattr__ is only called for attributes not found in the instance's dict or class. Since fileno is not defined in class, __getattr__ should forward to underlying file. So why does fileno raise UnsupportedOperation? Let's consider: sys.stdout replaced with FileProxy (subclass of io.TextIOBase). If you call sys.stdout.fileno(), Python will find fileno method in the base class io.TextIOBase? Look at io.TextIOBase definition: I think io.TextIOBase defines a fileno method that raises OSError (UnsupportedOperation). Indeed, TextIOBase implements fileno that raises UnsupportedOperation. Because FileProxy inherits from TextIOBase, the fileno attribute exists (inherited) and __getattr__ is not called because attribute name exists. Therefore calling fileno uses the default that raises. To fix, we can override fileno in FileProxy to delegate to underlying file's fileno (if any). So modify file_proxy.py to add def fileno(self): return self.__file.fileno().
